The published incidence of progressive pulmonary fibrosis in CTD-ILD is 29% (95% CI 25-34): Frontiers in Immunology 2026;17:1758437, doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1758437 (PMID 41716405, PMC12913582), a systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 studies, 20 of them rated high quality on the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, covering 3,224 CTD-ILD patients
column12: a single sourced share, not a stack of judgements. The meta-analysis is mostly non-US cohorts and its by-disease rates vary widely (32% in Sjogren's, 19% in SSc, 18% in SLE), so the pooled figure is used rather than a weighted recombination the source does not support

column11: a judgement, and the competitive case is this. Nintedanib is approved for chronic fibrosing ILD with a progressive phenotype and is the incumbent the trial's population is already failing or tolerating badly; tocilizumab is approved in SSc-ILD but not here; mycophenolate and rituximab are used off label. Belimumab would be the first B-cell-pathway agent with a label in this population, and it arrives as an add-on to standard therapy rather than a replacement, which widens use but caps share. Set against that, belimumab's own penetration in its approved disease is modest: 5,831 Part D plus 3,685 Part B Medicare beneficiaries in 2024 against a CDC-registry US lupus prevalence of 204,295
